A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RayRoPE work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original LVSM and EscherNet novel-view synthesis experiments, UniMatch stereo-depth experiments, ablations, generalization tests, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds TokenGS reconstruction experiments and Objaverse ablation results.

M1.justification: The core RayRoPE procedure remains unchanged. However, the new TokenGS adaptation in v3 Section 5.3 and Appendix B changes latent-query cross-attention: it skips query-frame projection and applies ray encoding only to image features in global coordinates because the Gaussian query tokens lack explicit positions.

E1.justification: v3 adds feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction through TokenGS, substantially extending task coverage beyond image synthesis and stereo-depth estimation. DL3DV-10K was already used for EscherNet in v2; the addition concerns reconstruction of an explicit scene representation, not a previously unused dataset. Earlier coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 5 introduces original TokenGS as an evaluated comparator, alongside a PRoPE adaptation using the same latent-query treatment. Comparator membership in the retained LVSM, EscherNet, UniMatch, and runtime comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added TokenGS experiment introduces a distinct protocol: training with four views, 150K iterations at 256×256 with 1024 Gaussian tokens, then 10K iterations at 256×448 with 4096 tokens, followed by evaluation with 2, 4, and 6 views and test-time tuning. These are settings for a new experiment; existing evaluation protocols are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v3 Table 2 extends the four existing component ablations to Objaverse; v2 Table 4 reported only CO3D and RE10K. The questions tested remain uncertainty modeling, depth adaptiveness, multiple frequencies, and value/output encoding. Existing depth, attention-similarity, pose-variation, and generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.1 newly states that models are trained with three random seeds and mean results are reported, except for the large-scale experiments. v2 provides no corresponding run-count statement. This is newly disclosed statistical reporting, not evidence that the number of runs increased; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v3 adds quantitative and qualitative results for the new reconstruction task (Table 5 and Figure 9). With four input views, TokenGS PSNR is 22.85 for the original model, 23.04 with PRoPE, and 23.40 with RayRoPE. It also adds Objaverse ablation scores, including PSNR 20.37 without uncertainty versus 22.42 for full RayRoPE. Matched performance tables from v2 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The attention equations, uniform-distribution assumption, expected-RoPE derivation, and Appendix A.2 proof retain their mathematical substance. Section 4.2 rewrites projection using lifted 4×4 matrices and normalized homogeneous coordinates, yielding the same six-dimensional representation; this is an equivalent reformulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the claimed empirical applicability to feed-forward 3DGS reconstruction and emphasize integration into generic multi-view models. The central contribution—ray-based positional encoding satisfying the four stated desiderata—and the existing performance claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix B explains why the TokenGS latent-query adaptation uses global coordinates and does not preserve SE(3) invariance. Section 5.3 also newly interprets the retained EscherNet results as evidence that depth predictions tolerate diffusion noise. The limitations concerning uncertain cameras and unposed inputs remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds TokenGS configuration and training details and newly discloses EscherNet's three training reference views, 70K iterations, and batch size 32. Conversely, v3 omits v2's three-corner-ray implementation note and RTX A6000 runtime-profiling disclosure. These omissions do not establish actual implementation or hardware changes; the project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted references for TokenGS, Gaussian Splatting, acceleration, and camera-control methods such as ReRoPE. Section 2 qualifies the comparison with Positional Encoding Field as lacking exploration beyond two views. Unified Camera Positional Encoding and LLaVA-3D citations are removed, while the central positioning against CaPE, GTA, and PRoPE remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: runtime discussion moves from the appendix into Section 4.4, known-depth material is consolidated with analysis, and stereo depth and EscherNet join TokenGS under Broader Applications. The introduction gains an explicit contribution list, and prose and captions are revised throughout.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, restructures the ablation, depth, and known-depth tables, and extensively relocates figures. v3 Figure 3 combines the attention diagram with runtime curves while omitting the separate three-view timing bars. A new TokenGS table and qualitative figure are added; other qualitative images and generalization plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The TokenGS study adds useful evidence of transfer to latent 3D representations, while Objaverse ablations strengthen support for the design choices. Newly disclosed seed counts and training settings improve transparency. These are incremental gains over v2's already broad evaluation, partly offset by losing the corner-ray implementation note and runtime-hardware specification.
